questions.q: Does Athena maintain its own separate metadata store apart from the Glue Data Catalog?
options: No — Athena resolves table names by reading the Glue Data Catalog directly
Yes, Athena syncs a private copy of the Catalog every hour
Yes, but only for Parquet tables
Athena requires a manual export/import step from Glue before it can query anything
questions.explain: Athena has no independent metadata store — it looks table definitions up directly in the shared Glue Data Catalog.

questions.q: How long after a Glue crawler finishes writing a new table does it typically take for that table to become queryable in Athena?
options: Essentially immediately — there is no sync delay because Athena reads the Catalog directly
Up to 24 hours, due to a nightly sync job
It never becomes queryable without a manual 'publish to Athena' step
Only after the next Athena service restart
questions.explain: Because Athena reads the Catalog directly with no caching of its own, a newly written table is immediately queryable.

questions.q: What happens to Athena queries against a table if that table's entry is dropped from the Glue Data Catalog?
options: They fail immediately, since there is no cached fallback
They continue working using a cached copy for 24 hours
They automatically fall back to querying a different table
Nothing changes because Athena stores its own separate schema
questions.explain: Since Athena has no independent metadata store, dropping the Catalog entry breaks queries against it right away.

questions.q: If a crawler's registered schema drifts from what's actually in the underlying S3 files, what does Athena do?
options: It trusts whatever the Catalog currently says, since it has no independent way to verify against the real files beyond query time
It automatically corrects the schema to match the files
It refuses to run any query until the mismatch is fixed
It silently ignores the Catalog and infers schema fresh on every query
questions.explain: Athena relies on the Catalog's current definition — if it's out of sync with the real files, queries reflect the Catalog, not the files.

questions.q: Why can a table registered by one team be queried immediately by another team's Athena queries, with no explicit data-sharing step?
options: Because the Catalog is one shared store and visibility depends on IAM permissions, not data movement
Because AWS automatically emails all account users when a new table is created
Because every Catalog table is public by default across all AWS accounts
Because Athena physically duplicates the data into each team's own bucket
questions.explain: Since the Catalog is a single shared metadata store, cross-team visibility is governed by IAM permissions rather than any sync or sharing step.
